text:
li: FYI - launchpad-int8 canary is spiking structured-output parse errors on our funcall suite. Saw a jump from 0.3% -> 1.8% after the int8 build. Mostly truncated JSON arrays and occasional stray commas.

omar: Was this the new quant recipe with per-channel scales + bias folding?

li: Yep, recipe v3.2 (symmetric per-channel, improved clamping). FP16 mirror shows baseline ~0.35%. launchpad-int8 at 1.8% on 3k samples.

sasha: Can you paste an example failure (trimmed)?

li: Example:```INVOKE 1799123449 model=launchpad-int8 prompt_id=zz9 status=200 tokens=210 out_tail=...,"tools": [{"name": "save", "args": ["/tmp/log.txt"]},\n]``` Notice trailing `,\n]` and missing closing object.

ana: (should be ana) I'll run a mirroring replay to fp16 and a disabled-CB mirror. If CB (continuous batching) is the culprit we should see error drop.

omar: Also run token-id diffs for the prompt set between fp16 vocab and the quantized vocab; sometimes quant build accidentally reorders the tokenizer table.

li: Quick repro command I used:```for i in {1..3000}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/invoke -d '{"model":"launchpad-int8","prompt":"<funcall test>","max_tokens":256}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY'; done | jq -r '.out' | grep -E 'trunc|parse' -c``` Yields the counts above.

ana: I kicked mirror replay to fp16 and spun a no-CB mirror on the canary pool. Will report after 20m.

sasha: If mirror+no-CB reduces it, add a soft-parse retry in the canary route and hold rollout. If not, we need a quant-bisect (scale/table diff) + runtime kernel check (EOS handling).

deploy-bot: Canary launchpad-int8 -> 30% rolled at 1799123000, link: https://deploys.redwood/1799123000

omar: Suggest running a small kvcache-boundary simulator: take canonical prompts, simulate prefix lengths seen in canary traces, and inject kernel EOS elision scenario. That helped root cause a similar case last quarter.

li: Update (18m): No-CB mirror dropped parse-rate to 0.5% on 2k samples. FP16 mirror steady at 0.32%. Single automatic JSON-repair retry in proxy reduces effective failure to 0.22%.

omar: That strongly implicates an interaction between CB batching boundaries and the int8 runtime path. We had a micro-optimization that coalesces EOS tokens for speed in quant path. Might be clipping final bytes when sequence lengths align with a micro-block.

sasha: Operational action items: 1) pause further rollout, 2) add kvcache-boundary simulation to int8 onboard checks, 3) temporarily disable EOS coalescing in int8 runtime for canaries, 4) keep the soft-repair retry for the route.

li: Filing a short incident note with sample traces and steps to reproduce. Will attach canary logs + token-id diffs.

ana: I'll take the token-id diff and the onboard test hook. Planning to flip the CB-disable policy for new int8 canaries until the boundary check passes.

li: Thanks team. Will post the incident link shortly. :pray:
